Editing a step-invalid numeric param silently applies a HARDCODED DEFAULT instead of the typed value. Chain, all live-observed: (1) #nn-learning-rate-input is dbc.Input(type=number, step=0.001, min=0.0001, max=1) at dashboard_manager.py:979-988, min from MIN_LEARNING_RATE=0.0001 (canopy_constants.py:112). (3) A user edit of an invalid-valued number input gives Dash State None (callback body carried None across a 12s window; exactly 1 fire, no corrective fire). (4) The dirty tracker sees None != store, ENABLES Apply and shows '⚠️ Unsaved changes' -- the UI says the edit is pending. (5) _apply_parameters_handler substitutes the default for None: dashboard_manager.py:6975 "float(nn_lr) if nn_lr is not None else TrainingConstants.DEFAULT_LEARNING_RATE" (=0.01, canopy_constants.py:111). LIVE INSTANCE: /api/state 0.0789 -> user types 0.0733 -> Apply -> server log POSTs nn_learning_rate 0.01 -> /api/state 0.01. Neither the typed nor the prior value. SCOPE: the same 'is not None else DEFAULT' idiom covers ~18 numeric fields at :6973-6999, and a live DOM sweep found 7 of 22 sidebar number inputs whose OWN backend-seeded value is already stepMismatch -- nn-max-iterations (1000000/min 1/step 100), nn-max-total-epochs (114000/10/1000), nn-learning-rate (0.01/0.0001/0.001), nn-growth-preset-epochs (50/1/10), nn-dataset-elements (1000/50/100), cn-correlation-threshold (0.01/0.00001/0.0001), cn-training-convergence-threshold (0.001/0.000001/0.00001). BOUNDED: programmatic seeding and the Apply blur-commit are SAFE even off-grid -- two controls with an off-grid non-default LR (0.0789) preserved it through a dropdown-only Apply with and without the LR field focused. The corruption requires a USER EDIT of the field, i.e. exactly the panel's intended use. Fix target: align each field's min to its step grid (or drop min to a grid-consistent value / set step='any'), and make the None branch keep the backend value or refuse, not silently substitute a default.
